title: Expected Mac Has Automatic Security Updates Disabled
exclusions: Compares expected Macs with the Apple operating-system query value for whether automatic security updates—System Settings' installation of system data files and security updates—are enabled. It reports false, unknown, older-than-24-hour, or missing-within-48-hour state. Apple documents XProtect security-configuration updates as part of this background mechanism, but an enabled preference does not prove the newest XProtect payload installed, Gatekeeper policy is enforced, malware was blocked/remediated, or a particular update succeeded. The obsolete undocumented bundle-path/version-age and erroneous seconds-as-days logic were removed.
evidence: Retain `expected_macos_automatic_security_updates_disabled`, schedule/results/alerts; expected-device and exception lookup revisions; redacted MDM query responses with automatic-security-update boolean, command/response and collection times; API/collector health; fixtures; dashboard/case; and restored true state plus separate update evidence. This documentation-only review changed no setting, queried no device, and observed no XProtect payload.

controlTest.positiveScenario: At 2026-07-29T12:00:00Z add expected IDs `asu-off`, `asu-stale`, `asu-missing`. Index `asu-off` at 11:00 with `automatic_security_updates_enabled=false`; `asu-stale` true at 2026-07-28T11:59:59Z; and nothing for missing. Expect exactly `automatic_security_updates_disabled`, `status_stale` age 86401, and `not_observed_in_48h`.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Require zero rows for true state exactly 86400 seconds old or newer; inactive/future/expired/non-macOS inventory; unexpected observed IDs; or an exact future exception with reason, ticket, and owner. Expiry equal to dispatch does not suppress. A true preference with a failed/pending XProtect update remains outside this rule.

dataSources: Apple MDM operating-system/device-information query whose documented result corresponds to “Install system data files and security updates,” exported through the management service's supported API. Normalize `_time`, exact `device_id`, `platform`, boolean `automatic_security_updates_enabled`, `response_status`, `command_id`, `collector_time`, `tenant`, and `collector_version`. `index=endpoint_posture`, `sourcetype=local:apple:update_settings`, aliases, and lookups are local conventions. Collect declarative software-update status/error and actual XProtect/background-update evidence separately; do not parse undocumented XProtect bundle paths as an authoritative fleet API.
app: Apple device management and the chosen MDM vendor provide the update-setting query. A deployment-owned collector and Splunk search app provide normalization, expected inventory, exceptions, fixtures, search, dashboard, and runbook. Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (Splunkbase 833) is not a macOS XProtect source for this UC.
spl:
| inputlookup expected_macos_security_updates.csv
| eval device_id=lower(trim(device_id)), platform=lower(trim(platform)), monitor_from_epoch=tonumber(monitor_from_epoch), monitor_until_epoch=tonumber(monitor_until_epoch), expected_row=1
| where lower(trim(monitor_enabled))="true" AND platform="macos" AND len(device_id)>0 AND monitor_from_epoch<=now() AND monitor_until_epoch>now()
| fields device_id expected_row device_name serial_number owner criticality runbook
| append [ search index=endpoint_posture sourcetype=local:apple:update_settings earliest=-48h latest=now
    | eval device_id=lower(trim(device_id)), platform=lower(trim(platform)), automatic_security_updates_enabled=case(automatic_security_updates_enabled=true() OR lower(trim(automatic_security_updates_enabled))="true",1,automatic_security_updates_enabled=false() OR lower(trim(automatic_security_updates_enabled))="false",0,true(),null()), observed_row=1
    | where platform="macos" AND len(device_id)>0
    | stats latest(_time) AS status_time latest(automatic_security_updates_enabled) AS automatic_security_updates_enabled latest(response_status) AS response_status latest(command_id) AS command_id latest(collector_time) AS collector_time by device_id ]
| stats max(expected_row) AS expected_row max(observed_row) AS observed_row values(device_name) AS device_name values(serial_number) AS serial_number values(owner) AS owner values(criticality) AS criticality values(runbook) AS runbook max(status_time) AS status_time max(automatic_security_updates_enabled) AS automatic_security_updates_enabled values(response_status) AS response_status values(command_id) AS command_id max(collector_time) AS collector_time by device_id
| where expected_row=1
| eval status_age_seconds=if(isnull(status_time),null(),now()-status_time), finding=case(isnull(observed_row),"not_observed_in_48h",isnull(automatic_security_updates_enabled),"unknown_update_setting",automatic_security_updates_enabled=0,"automatic_security_updates_disabled",status_age_seconds>86400,"status_stale",true(),"healthy")
| where finding!="healthy"
| lookup macos_security_update_exceptions.csv device_id OUTPUT exception_until_epoch exception_reason ticket exception_owner
| eval exception_until_epoch=tonumber(exception_until_epoch), exception_active=if(exception_until_epoch>now() AND len(exception_reason)>0 AND len(ticket)>0 AND len(exception_owner)>0,1,0)
| where exception_active=0
| eval stale_threshold_seconds=86400, observation_window_hours=48, observation_semantics="preference_state_not_XProtect_payload_freshness_or_Gatekeeper_attestation", use_case_id="UC-1.3.6"
| table device_id device_name serial_number finding automatic_security_updates_enabled status_time status_age_seconds response_status command_id collector_time owner criticality runbook stale_threshold_seconds observation_window_hours observation_semantics use_case_id
| sort 0 finding -status_age_seconds device_id
description: Runs daily and emits one row per active expected Mac when the latest MDM-reported automatic-security-update setting is absent for 48 hours, unknown, false, or strictly older than 24 hours. The grain is exact lowercased device-management ID, with command, collection, lifecycle, and owner context.
value: Disabling automatic security-configuration updates can delay XProtect and other system security data, while stale/absent status hides whether the preference is governed. The result gives endpoint teams a precise settings gap without inventing an unsupported XProtect-definition age or conflating Gatekeeper policy with update delivery.
implementation: Collect the documented automatic-security-update setting through MDM, preserve command/API health, normalize booleans without guessing, and reconcile exact expected devices. Run daily with 48-hour observation and 24-hour freshness, use finite exact exceptions, and alert by device/finding. Verify update settings and actual background/XProtect update outcomes separately before closure; manage Gatekeeper through its security payload control.
visualization: Show query/collector freshness, response failures, expected coverage, unknowns, and duplicate IDs first. Then display disabled/stale/absent by owner/site/model and trend setting changes. Drill down to redacted MDM response, software-update configuration/status/error, Apple background-update evidence, exception, case, and restored state. Label the panel preference state—not XProtect currency.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable; no CIM mapping is asserted for Apple automatic-security-update preference or XProtect payload freshness.

knownFalsePositives:
A finding is real setting/visibility evidence but can reflect an approved temporary state.

1. **Compatibility troubleshooting** — An owner may temporarily pause system data/security updates during a documented incident. Confirm exact device, reason, risk, start/end, compensating control, and restoration test.

2. **MDM migration or re-enrollment** — Device ID and query history can change. Reconcile serial, old/new IDs, tenant, enrollment, and asset lifecycle before editing inventory.

3. **Query/API/collector failure** — Permission, command timeout, pagination, or indexing failure causes stale/absent rows. Check canary, response/command ID, totals, collector time, and MDM console before endpoint action.

4. **Vendor normalization mismatch** — Some services expose a nested update-settings object or null on unsupported releases. Verify vendor schema, supported OS, raw redacted response, parser version, and fixture; do not map missing to false.

**Suppression mechanism:** the SPL uses `lookup macos_security_update_exceptions.csv` on exact `device_id` and requires future expiry, reason, ticket, and owner. Expired, wildcard, fleet-wide, collector-outage, Gatekeeper-policy, or XProtect-payload exceptions do not suppress.

detailedImplementation:
## Source contract and policy boundary

Assign MDM, macOS security/update, asset, Splunk, service-desk, and change owners. Qualify the device-management query across supported releases; this review ran none. Apple documents an operating-system query that returns whether “Install system data files and security updates” is on. Apple also documents XProtect updates as automatically delivered security-configuration/system-data updates. That supports a settings control—not the previous claim that `system_profiler` or an undocumented bundle date proves XProtect freshness.

Export exact device/tenant/command identity, query boolean, response status, device status time, API collection time, pagination, and collector version. Normalize true/false/null using vendor-schema fixtures. Create `expected_macos_security_updates.csv` with unique device ID, macOS platform, lifecycle epochs, serial, owner, criticality, and runbook. Reconcile MDM/asset state daily. Create `macos_security_update_exceptions.csv` with exact ID and finite approval.

Monitor query success, command errors, canary, object/page totals, duplicate IDs, null rate by OS, event/index delay, and collector version. Separately ingest declarative software-update status/errors where supported and maintain an approved method to inspect actual security-configuration/background-update outcomes. Do not store a guessed `xprotect_date` or divide raw seconds incorrectly.

## Search, tests, and alerting

Save `expected_macos_automatic_security_updates_disabled` and schedule daily. Inventory-first logic detects absence; exact 86400 seconds is fresh. Route broad stale/missing waves to MDM/data owners before endpoint responders. Trigger by device/finding and include source-health and update-status drilldowns.

Run fixed controls plus true/false/null/string, 86399/86400/86401 ages, no observation, duplicate/newer state, wrong platform, unsupported OS, lifecycle/exception equality, MDM migration, API failure, delayed indexing, and preference toggling in a managed lab. Verify the MDM result against System Settings and vendor documentation. A true setting must not clear a fixture representing failed/pending actual update status. Keep draft until owners accept versions, source semantics, freshness, tests, alert delivery, and response.

## Response and troubleshooting

Verify collector/query health and a canary; exact identity/lifecycle; latest response and supported OS; MDM-enforced Software Update settings; device network/power/storage; deferral/restriction policy; actual background-update and declarative status/error; and recent compatibility incident. Determine whether this is disabled preference, unsupported/missing field, collection failure, or update-delivery failure.

Do not automatically toggle updates, invoke `softwareupdate` or `xprotect`, change Gatekeeper, remove a security update, restart, or re-enroll from Splunk. Use staged MDM change control and application compatibility review. Close this rule after a fresh true query; close the operational risk only after separate evidence that relevant background/security updates are current and functioning. If true but XProtect evidence is stale, route the separate update-delivery control; if Gatekeeper policy is weak, route the security-payload control; if every device is missing, repair the collector.
grandmaExplanation: We check whether each expected Mac is still set to receive Apple’s background security data, including XProtect updates. The setting being on is useful, but we verify actual update delivery separately.
